items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: my long time friend Edgar Courance who had acquired the name of Spider... Freddie had told me in New York who were the other two musicians that were coming with us.

ctx.x: I think the sailing time for the "Normandie" was 10 a.m. and I had to see my buddy Dick Wells before I left. I have not even written him from Cincinnati to let him know that I was going to Europe although I was certain that he would have kept it a secret if I had asked him. But I just wasn't taking any chances. So we came from Leonia early in the morning of the 25th and I woke Dickie up about 8 and told him what was happening. He was real happy to see me. I told him why I had left New York which he did not know…

Freddie had told me in New York who were the other two musicians that were coming with us. George Johnson who had played in Benny Carter's 1933 band and my long time friend Edgar Courance who had acquired the name of Spider because he was working in a club by that name when Freddy had approached him about going to Europe.

Spider told me later that he was not too enthused about going to France when Freddie asked him. He asked Freddie who else was going and Freddie broke the promise he had made to me and told Edgar that I would be the trumpet man. He asked Edgar not to say anything about me going to anyone else and Spider accepted to go after he knew that I was going.
